tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichl.summary: Tau Ceti has built most of this roadmap: `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ArithmeticDirichletSeries/` holds 665 sorry-free declarations across 28 files, and Layers 0–4 are complete in the stated generality — the nonzero-ideal carrier with its zero extension, both completely multiplicative weight carriers with all constructors and the three rejection tests, `normCoeff` and `regroupByNorm`, ideal convolution with Möbius inversion and the von Mangoldt transform, `EulerProductData` with the analytic Euler product and a holomorphic branch of its logarithm, and the counting carriers with `primeTheta`, `primeCount` and `primePsi`. Layer 5 is complete but for the named density-zero corollary for degree-above-one primes, Layer 8 for the ordinary-versus-absolute abscissa equality (which no library can state, having no ordinary abscissa), and Layer 6 for the cancellation package `HasCancellation`/`continuedLFunctionOfWeight`; the arithmetic Perron formula that the roadmap's own STATUS.md calls untouched is in fact proved, as are the analytic Euler product, the log-derivative identity and the meromorphic Landau corollary. What is genuinely missing is a connected block: Wiener–Ikehara's final Tauberian step (the smoothed asymptotic with derived Chebyshev growth is done, the passage to `x⁻¹ ∑_{n≤x} a n → κ` is not), the whole Dirichlet-density calculus of Layer 7 beyond the base Mathlib API the pinned revision already supplies, and consequently `PrimeBoundaryRemainder`, `primePsi_asymptotic_of_boundary` and the summit `primeNumberTheoremTransfer`. Mathlib contributes the ambient `LSeries`, `ArithmeticFunction`, `EulerProduct`, `AbelSummation` and `NumberField.Set.HasDirichletDensity` APIs but nothing ideal-indexed and no Tauberian theorem.

targets.target: `IdealArithmeticFunction K`: complex-valued functions on the nonzero ideals `(Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰`
targets.note: An `abbrev` for `(Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰ → ℂ`, exactly the carrier the layer asks for; the coprime-multiplicativity predicate sits beside it. Mathlib has no ideal-indexed arithmetic-function carrier of its own (`ArithmeticFunction` is `ℕ`-indexed).

targets.target: canonical `zeroExtend` to all integral ideals; the extension vanishes exactly at `⊥` when the original never vanishes
targets.note: `zeroExtend_ne_zero` is precisely the 'zero exactly at ⊥ when `f` has no zero values' statement; the `restrict`/`zeroExtend` pair is proved to be a bijection onto functions vanishing at `⊥`.

targets.target: `MultiplicativeIdealWeight K` via `Ideal (𝓞 K) →*₀ ℂ` with a finite bad set of height-one primes
targets.note: Built on Mathlib's `MonoidWithZeroHom` vocabulary, so `apply_bot` is inherited from `map_zero` exactly as the layer specifies.

targets.target: `UnitaryIdealWeight K` as the unit-modulus subtype away from the bad set
targets.note: A subtype of `MultiplicativeIdealWeight` with modulus one on good ideals, as stated.

targets.target: constructors and operations: trivial weight, conjugation, pointwise product, restriction away from a finite prime set, norm twists, finite-order weights
targets.note: `ofPowEqOne` is the finite-order constructor landing in `UnitaryIdealWeight`; `UnitaryIdealWeight.normTwist` (Weight.lean:681) is the imaginary twist that stays unitary, while the general `MultiplicativeIdealWeight.normTwist` is the arbitrary one. Pointwise product is the monoid `mul_apply` (Weight.lean:253), kept separate from ideal convolution.

targets.target: maps to `IdealArithmeticFunction` and functoriality under a number-field equivalence
targets.note: Transport along `K ≃+* L` exists on all three carriers with `map_id`/`map_map` and compatibility with `one`, `mul`, `restrict`, `conj` and `normTwist`.

targets.target: the zero-ideal rejection test: the everywhere-one function on all ideals is no zero extension and underlies neither weight carrier; a twist with `Re z ≠ 0` fails unitarity on good ideals of norm > 1
targets.note: All three required worked rejection examples are proved theorems, not remarks.

targets.target: finite norm fibres of the absolute norm on nonzero ideals
targets.note: Mathlib supplies finiteness for an arbitrary ring of integers; Tau Ceti packages the fibre as a `Finset` of `(Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰`, which is what the summation needs.

targets.target: `normCoeff f : ArithmeticFunction ℂ` by summing over the norm fibre, with values at 0 and 1, conjugation, norm twists and field equivalence
targets.note: The value at `0` is definitional (`ArithmeticFunction` carrier); `normCoeff_mul_absNorm_cpow` is the general norm twist and `MultiplicativeIdealWeight.normCoeff_normTwist` (Weight.lean:413) / `UnitaryIdealWeight.normCoeff_normTwist` (Weight.lean:835) the weight-level versions. The roadmap's STATUS.md lists the twist and field-equivalence compatibilities as 'not visible'; at this baseline they are.

targets.target: `regroupByNorm`: ideal-indexed absolute convergence implies `LSeriesSummable (normCoeff f) s` with equal sum; abscissa comparison; converse under ideal-summand nonnegativity
targets.note: The converse is proved exactly under nonnegativity of every ideal summand, and `exists_forall_normCoeff_nonneg_not_forall_nonneg` (NormCoeff.lean:216) is the counterexample showing nonnegative grouped coefficients do not suffice.

targets.target: trivial specialization: `normCoeff` of the trivial weight is the Dedekind-zeta coefficient; the coefficient is 1 for every positive integer over `ℚ`
targets.note: Matches the layer, including the `K = ℚ` specialization; the exact abscissa is deliberately deferred to Layer 5, as the roadmap requires.

duplicates.note: AN.0 asks in one line for 'arithmetic functions, absolute convergence, ... partial summation' over ℚ; this layer is the number-field-ideal refinement of the same carrier, and AN.0 is a specification with no Lean content.

targets.target: ideal convolution on `IdealArithmeticFunction K` with associativity, commutativity, delta identity, distributivity, iterated powers
targets.note: Defined by the finite divisor antidiagonal of a nonzero ideal, codomain again `IdealArithmeticFunction`, exactly as specified.

targets.target: `normCoeff_convolution`: transport to Mathlib Dirichlet convolution in `ArithmeticFunction ℂ`
targets.note: Identifies `normCoeff (f ⋆ g)` with the product in Mathlib's `ArithmeticFunction ℂ`; `convolution_one_one_ne_mul` (Convolution.lean:378) is the recorded warning that pointwise product is different.

targets.target: ideal Möbius function: prime-power values, convolution inverse of the constant one, multiplicativity on coprime ideals, and rejection from both weight carriers
targets.note: `convolution_one_eq_iff` is the Möbius-inversion equivalence; the unitary rejection is `not_exists_unitaryIdealWeight_eq_moebius` (Moebius.lean:348). Both the positive multiplicativity statement and the rejection theorem are exported, as demanded.

targets.target: ideal von Mangoldt weight, its transform attached to a weight, support on prime powers, and the exact log-derivative coefficient identity on the absolute-convergence half-plane
targets.note: `logDeriv L(s) = -∑' A, χ(A) Λ(A) / N(A)^s` strictly right of `idealAbscissaOfAbsConv`, which is exactly 2.3. The roadmap's own STATUS.md (2026-09-01) records 2.3 as lacking this identity; at this baseline it is proved, sorry-free.

targets.target: `EulerProductData` storing coprime multiplicativity, prime-power local series and the finite bad set, extending Mathlib's `ArithmeticFunction.ofPowerSeries`/`eulerProduct` and `EulerProduct`
targets.note: Extensionality, product (`mul_apply` 162), unit (`one_apply` 170), conjugation (`star_apply` 203), restriction and the trivial-weight instance are all present, and the file builds on Mathlib's `EulerProduct`/`ArithmeticFunction.eulerProduct` rather than duplicating them. The roadmap's STATUS.md records that 'nothing named EulerProductData exists'; at this baseline it does.

targets.target: factorization of a coefficient over the prime-power factorization of a nonzero ideal; equality for Euler products over a finite set of primes
targets.note: The formal coefficientwise product and the analytic finite product over a `Finset` of height-one primes are separate named theorems.

targets.target: infinite Euler product under absolute convergence, identified with `LSeries (normCoeff f)`, with nonvanishing where the reciprocal product converges
targets.note: `HasProd` over the height-one primes in the unrestricted sense, hypothesis exactly absolute convergence of the ideal-indexed series; nonvanishing is stated pointwise only, as the roadmap insists. STATUS.md records 3.3 as 'formal only' — it is no longer.

targets.target: a holomorphic logarithm on a simply connected zero-free region, with the prime-power expansion and its derivative
targets.note: The branch is chosen on a simply connected open set of absolute convergence, and the principal logarithm is deliberately not applied to the product — exactly the 3.4 discipline. STATUS.md records 3.4 as untouched; at this baseline it is proved.

duplicates.note: AN.0's 'Euler products ... with convergence proofs' is the same target over ℚ, at specification level only.
AL.4 builds unramified local L-factors for general L-groups; the degree-one ideal Euler factor here is the `GL(1)` case, and this roadmap is AL's declared supplier.

targets.target: cutoff subtypes of ideals, height-one primes and prime powers with `absNorm ≤ x`; finiteness, monotonicity, real/natural cutoff equivalence, empty small cutoffs
targets.note: Finiteness comes from a Northcott instance for `Ideal.absNorm` on `(Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰` (Counting.lean:101), which in turn rests on Mathlib's `Ideal.finite_setOf_absNorm_le`. `primesLE_eq_empty_of_lt_two` and `primePowersLE_eq_empty_of_lt_two` give the small-cutoff cases.

targets.target: generic inclusive summatory functions on ideals, primes and prime powers for nonnegative real weights, with additivity, monotonicity and invariance under modification on a finite set
targets.note: All three are instances of a single generic `TauCeti.summatory` over a Northcott norm (TauCeti/Order/Northcott.lean); monotonicity and nonnegativity are at Counting.lean:424 and :429.

targets.target: `primeTheta` and `primeCount` for a set of height-one primes, with finite-union and finite-symmetric-difference lemmas
targets.note: Inclusive real cutoffs with `primeTheta_eq_primeTheta_natFloor`/`primeCount_eq_primeCount_natFloor` (Counting.lean:685, :694) giving the natural-cutoff conversion; `eventually_primeCount_sub_eq` (:793) is the symmetric-difference lemma.

duplicates.note: Chebotarev 11.2 defines `ψ_C` and `ϑ_C` on 'the canonical prime subtype' — it specializes these carriers to a Frobenius fibre rather than redefining them, and cites them by name.

targets.target: two-sided linear bounds for the ideal count, packaged as `IdealCountingLinearBounds`, with `idealCount_linearBounds`
targets.note: The contract names are used verbatim; the bounds are positive and two-sided, as required for the divergence half of 5.1a.

targets.target: `abscissaOfAbsConv_normCoeff_one = 1`, proved from the two-sided counts and not from continuation
targets.note: Estimates.lean imports no continuation and no Dedekind pole; the divergence at `s = 1` comes from `lower_div_two_le_sum_Ioc_norm_term`. Noncircular exactly as the roadmap demands.

targets.target: generic `O(√x log² x)` estimate for higher prime powers under the standard logarithmic weight, with isolated hypotheses for other weights
targets.note: The `O(√x log² x)` bound is proved with an explicit constant, and the two `..._of_le_higherPrimePowerWeight` lemmas isolate exactly the domination hypothesis another weight must supply.

targets.target: convergence and density-zero statements for primes of residue degree above one
targets.note: The convergence statements are complete, including the bound on `primeIdealZetaSum` uniform in `s ≥ 1` that a Dirichlet-density-zero argument needs. What is missing is the density-zero statement itself: the Lean docstring at ResidueDegree.lean:160 says explicitly that `o(x / log x)` 'is not a statement of natural density zero' because the prime ideal theorem is unavailable, and there is no `HasDirichletDensity (higherDegreePrimes K) 0` either, since Layer 7's predicate does not exist yet.

targets.note: Mathlib's identity is consumed, not restated; Tau Ceti adds only the norm-indexed bridges (`normFiberSum`, AbelSummation.lean:67) and the ϑ↔π conversions, with the inclusive cutoff convention.

targets.target: `ϑ(x) ∼ δx ⟹ π(x) ∼ δ Li(x)`, `Li(x) ∼ x/log x`, and the zero-density case
targets.note: Both the `δ ≠ 0` equivalence and the `δ = 0` little-o form are separate named theorems, as the layer requires. Mathlib has no logarithmic integral; Tau Ceti defines it as `∫ t in 2..x, (log t)⁻¹`.

targets.target: `truncatedPerronKernel x c T` as a smoothed step with a proved universal error constant; exact value `π⁻¹ arctan(T/c)` at `x = 1` tending to `1/2`
targets.note: The `(2π)⁻¹` prefactor convention is the one in `perronIntegrand` (Perron/Basic.lean:75); `truncatedPerronKernel_one_ne_half` is the required endpoint rejection test.

targets.target: arithmetic Perron: interchange with an absolutely convergent `LSeries`, truncated summatory formula, off-norm and half-weight limiting forms
targets.note: Both required forms are present: the off-norm bound against the sharp partial sum, and the integer-endpoint limit with the half weight `f N / 2`. The contract row names this `perronFormula`; no declaration carries that name, but the mathematics is proved. STATUS.md records 6.4 as untouched; at this baseline it is done.

targets.target: `HasCancellation χ` (uniform `O(X^(1-1/[K:ℚ]))` for ideal partial sums) and `continuedLFunctionOfWeight χ` with agreement on `Re s > 1` and analyticity on `Re s > 1-1/[K:ℚ]`
targets.note: Neither name nor any equivalent statement appears in Mathlib or Tau Ceti: no declaration bounds ideal partial sums of a unitary weight by `X^(1-1/[K:ℚ])`, and no continuation of such an L-series into the strip exists. The Abel-summation input it would use (`summatory_mul_eq_sub_sub_integral_mul`) is available, so the gap is the analytic construction, not its machinery. The related good-ideal/conjugation/square/imaginary-twist operations on `UnitaryIdealWeight` do exist (Weight.lean:717–835).

targets.target: adopt Mathlib's `primeIdealZetaSum`, `HasDirichletDensity`, `dirichletDensity`
targets.note: The layer's first task is 'update the repository pin' to a Mathlib containing this file; the pinned baseline already contains it, so that task is done and is in any case process rather than mathematics. Mathlib supplies the ratio definition, the junk-valued density, emptiness, nonnegativity and `≤ 1`. Tau Ceti already adds two monotonicity lemmas in the same namespace (Convergence.lean:125, :137).

targets.note: Neither library defines one-sided Dirichlet-density bounds, and no union, squeeze, complement, finite-symmetric-difference or contraction lemma for `HasDirichletDensity` exists. The analogous calculus does exist for the *natural* density predicate Tau Ceti defines (`NumberField.Set.HasNaturalDensity.union`, `.compl`, `.of_finite_symmDiff`, `hasNaturalDensity_of_finite` in NaturalDensity.lean:112–176), so this is a transcription of an existing pattern to the Dirichlet side.

targets.target: the all-prime normalization `P_all(s) = log(1/(s-1)) + O(1)` and equivalence with logarithmic normalization
targets.note: Absent as a statement. The two prerequisites the roadmap names are now in place: the ideal Euler product of `ζ_K` on `Re s > 1`, and the uniform bound on the higher-degree-prime contribution. Mathlib has the rational-prime analogue only in spirit, via `Nat.Primes`-indexed Euler products; nothing states the `log(1/(s-1))` asymptotic for the number-field prime sum.

targets.target: density calculus: finite-set density zero, finite symmetric difference, monotonicity, complements, finite disjoint unions, squeeze, and the natural-to-Dirichlet implication with the named denominator hypothesis
targets.note: The whole calculus exists for `HasNaturalDensity` (defined by Tau Ceti as the ratio of prime counts) and none of it for `HasDirichletDensity`. `hasDirichletDensity_of_hasNaturalDensity` is absent, as is any `AllPrimeDirichletDenominatorAsymptotic` hypothesis carrier.

targets.target: Landau's theorem: nonnegative coefficients with `abscissaOfAbsConv a = (σ : EReal)` make `σ` a singularity of every continuation from `Re s > σ`
targets.note: The hypothesis is the Mathlib *equality* `LSeries.abscissaOfAbsConv a = (σ : EReal)`, verbatim what the layer requires; the proof is sorry-free and the file contains no `sorry`. Mathlib has no Landau theorem.

targets.target: the meromorphic-order corollary needed by nonvanishing arguments
targets.note: States that the forced singularity is a pole, not removable. STATUS.md lists this as 'not visible'; at this baseline it is proved.

targets.note: Mathlib defines only the abscissa of *absolute* convergence; no ordinary abscissa of convergence exists in either library (no `abscissaOfConv` anywhere), so the equality cannot even be stated yet. This is the one gap in an otherwise finished layer.

targets.target: the `3-4-1` trigonometric nonnegativity packaged as a finite nonnegative coefficient combination, with analytic input kept separate
targets.note: Packaged with no character data attached, exactly as the layer specifies; `3 + 4cos θ + cos 2θ = 2(1 + cos θ)²` is the proved identity behind it.

targets.target: the rejection test: the trivial weight and its nonzero norm twists do not have cancellation (linear partial sums, shifted Dedekind zeta with a pole)
targets.note: The ingredients are proved — the two-sided linear ideal count is exactly the statement that the trivial weight's partial sums are of linear size — but there is no declaration asserting the failure of `HasCancellation`, because `HasCancellation` itself does not exist (Layer 6.5).

What is missing is the last Tauberian step from the smoothed limit `∑ a n 𝓕ψ(log(n/x)/2π) → 2π A ψ(0)` to the sharp cutoff `x⁻¹ ∑_{n≤x} a n → κ`. No declaration named `wienerIkehara` exists in either library; Mathlib mentions Wiener–Ikehara only in a docstring in `Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/PrimesInAP.lean:253`. All four WienerIkehara files are sorry-free.

targets.note: Not present; it is a specialization of the missing summit.

targets.target: variants: natural cutoffs, finite changes of coefficients, a pole at a positive abscissa after rescaling, coefficients in an ordered real normed algebra
targets.note: None of the 9.2 variants exists. The natural-cutoff bridge on the arithmetic side (`primePsi_eq_sum_range`, Prime/Psi.lean:506) is in place, so the variant would be a restatement once the main theorem lands.

targets.note: Nonnegativity (`primeVonMangoldtCoeff_nonneg`, :448) and prime-power support (:477) are proved, and `primePsi_eq_sum_range` is exactly the bridge a Tauberian theorem consumes.

targets.note: Neither the structure nor the theorem exists; the only occurrence of the name in the whole baseline is a prose mention in the module docstring of Prime/Psi.lean:67. It cannot be discharged before Layer 9's `wienerIkehara`.

targets.target: `standardPrimePowerRemoval : HasNegligibleHigherPrimePowers K S` and `primeTheta_asymptotic_of_primePsi` consuming it
targets.note: Exactly the contract names, and the transfer theorem takes the named estimate as a hypothesis rather than reproving it; the generalized-weight route is `primePowerSummatory_isLittleO_of_le_higherPrimePowerWeight` (HigherPrimePowers.lean:374), which demands nonnegativity, support and the growth bound as the layer requires.

targets.target: `primeCount_asymptotic_of_primeTheta`, and the summit `primeNumberTheoremTransfer` returning `ψ`, `ϑ` and `π` from a `PrimeBoundaryRemainder`
targets.note: The ϑ-to-π leg is proved in both the `δ ≠ 0` and `δ = 0` forms. The summit itself does not exist: it needs the missing `PrimeBoundaryRemainder` and Layer 9.

targets.note: Neither exists. Producing the external input needs continuation of `ζ_K` past `Re s = 1` and nonvanishing on the line; the baseline proves nonvanishing only on the open half-plane `Re s > 1`, which is strictly weaker and exactly the gap the layer names.

AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli.summary: Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has an abelian scheme: the phrase does not occur in any Lean source in the baseline, and there is no base scheme, relative dimension, Picard functor, dual, polarization, Weil pairing, relative de Rham cohomology, Tate module, p-divisible group or Weil restriction anywhere. What exists is the field case and the linear-algebra shadow of the complex theory. Mathlib proves that a proper geometrically integral group scheme over a field is commutative (Stacks 0BFD) and that such a group scheme is smooth; Tau Ceti builds on those to define `AbelianVariety K` with dimension, zero section, base change along field extensions, products, hom groups, the endomorphism ring, isogenies and the tangent space at the identity, and separately has Cartier duality for finite locally free commutative affine group schemes — the one import A3 and A4 declare — together with a full polarized-Hodge-structure library that supplies the target category of A5's uniformization equivalence. Genuinely missing is almost everything the roadmap owns: the relative theory over a base, rigidity for pointed maps and the theorems of the square and cube, the Picard functor and the dual with Poincaré bundle and polarizations, torsion quotients and pairings, degree-one realizations and Serre–Tate, complex uniformization with the Siegel family, and the arithmetic Hom/End theorems with Weil restriction. A1 is the only layer with real coverage, and only in the base = `Spec K` case; A0 is an explicit import boundary and is process rather than mathematics.

targets.target: import and reexport of `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry` R09.1–R09.6 and A0-extension: algebraic spaces, Hilbert/Picard representability, higher-dimensional coherent base change, Artin criteria
targets.note: The layer states outright that it 'is an import boundary, not a second construction' and that its producer row 'imports exactly those general stages and reexports their hypotheses and universal properties'. It contains no mathematical target of its own, so it is bookkeeping. For the record the imported objects are themselves absent: neither library has algebraic spaces, a Picard functor for schemes (no `Pic` of a scheme anywhere), a Hilbert functor, or Artin representability criteria.

duplicates.note: The owner of the imported general stages; A0 is by its own text only a reexport of it.

targets.target: abelian scheme over a general base: proper smooth group scheme with geometrically connected fibres, relative dimension locally constant on a possibly disconnected base
targets.note: Nothing in either library is an abelian scheme over a base: the string 'abelian scheme' does not occur in any Lean source, and no relative-dimension function exists. What exists is the base = `Spec K` case: `AbelianVariety K` bundles a proper geometrically integral group scheme over a field, from which smoothness (Mathlib's `smooth_of_grpObj`, itself for a group scheme over a field) and geometric connectedness are derived, and `dim` is the topological Krull dimension of the total space rather than a locally constant relative dimension.

targets.target: rigidity for pointed maps, and commutativity of the group law
targets.note: Mathlib proves commutativity (Stacks 0BFD) for a proper geometrically integral group scheme over a *field*; over a base it is absent. The rigidity lemma itself — a pointed map from a proper family constant on one fibre is constant — is not stated separately in either library, only this corollary, and neither is the nonreduced-base argument the layer demands.

targets.target: translation invariance of differentials; theorem of the square and of the cube
targets.note: Absent from both libraries: no occurrence of a theorem of the square, theorem of the cube, seesaw principle, or invariant differentials of a group scheme. Tau Ceti has the tangent space at the identity of an abelian variety with its finite-dimensionality (`AbelianVariety.TangentSpace`, TangentSpace.lean:85, and `finiteDimensional_tangentSpace`, :157) but no translation-invariance statement.

targets.target: homomorphisms as group-scheme homomorphisms; decomposition of a map into a homomorphism and a translation; products and base change
targets.note: Over a field, homomorphisms are morphisms of group objects, form a commutative group under the pointwise law, and are stable under base change; products of abelian varieties are constructed with properness and geometric integrality of the product. `baseChange` is along a field extension `K → L`, not along an arbitrary base change of schemes. The hom-plus-translation decomposition is absent.

targets.target: one-dimensional pointed abelian schemes coincide with the scheme-theoretic elliptic curves, compatibly with the group laws
targets.note: Absent. Mathlib's `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/` is entirely Weierstrass models with point-set group laws (Affine, Projective, Jacobian); there is no elliptic curve as a group scheme in either library and therefore no equivalence to state.

duplicates.note: Layer E states the identical targets — 'abelian variety = smooth, proper, geometrically connected group scheme over `k`; basic API, `dim`. Commutativity is automatic (rigidity, `Group/Abelian.lean`)' — over a field, and is the layer whose targets Tau Ceti has actually built.

targets.target: the relative degree-zero Picard functor as an algebraic space
targets.note: No Picard functor, Picard scheme or `Pic` of a scheme exists in either library — the only `Picard` declarations in Mathlib are `IsPicardLindelof` for ODEs. Algebraic spaces are absent too. Tau Ceti has invertible sheaves and their tensor product (`TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheaf`, LineBundle/Basic.lean:78; `LineBundleClass`, LineBundle/Class.lean:49) but no Picard group functor.

targets.target: Raynaud's abelian-algebraic-space-to-scheme theorem (Faltings–Chai I.1.9) with its actual base hypotheses, and the dual abelian scheme
targets.note: Absent. No dual abelian variety or scheme exists in either library.

targets.target: rigidified Poincaré bundle and the biduality isomorphism
targets.note: Absent; no Poincaré bundle in either library.

targets.target: `φ_L : A → A∨` from a line bundle, its behaviour under tensor product, translation and pullback, the positivity condition defining a polarization, symmetric homomorphisms, Rosati involutions and polarization types

AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.summary: Nothing this roadmap owns exists in either library. The decisive gap is at the very bottom: there is no étale fundamental group of a scheme anywhere in the baseline — Mathlib's `CategoryTheory/Galois/` develops Galois categories, fibre functors, Galois objects, prorepresentability and `IsFundamentalGroup` in the abstract, but the phrase 'finite étale' does not occur in `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/`, and the only instantiation of that abstract theory is Tau Ceti's topological one for finite covering spaces. Without it there are no path torsors, no Galois sections, no unipotent quotients and no Selmer varieties; independently, `Chabauty`, `Coleman`, `iteratedIntegral`, `NeronSeveri` and `anabelian` each have zero occurrences in the whole baseline, and there is no p-adic height, no de Rham or rigid cohomology of a curve, no nonabelian `H¹`, and no Jacobian. The genuinely usable inputs are Mathlib's abstract Galois-category API and low-degree abelian group cohomology, and Tau Ceti's Tannakian and unipotent-algebraic-group machinery, which would be the target category of NC.2. NC.6 is an export and conditionality-bookkeeping layer with no mathematics of its own.

targets.target: the finite-étale fibre functor and the Galois category of finite étale covers of a scheme, with its profinite automorphism group
targets.note: Mathlib has the abstract theory — Galois categories, fibre functors, Galois objects, prorepresentability, the equivalence with continuous finite `Aut F`-sets and the `IsFundamentalGroup` predicate — but no instance of it for finite étale covers of a scheme. The words 'finite étale' do not appear in `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/`, and neither library defines an étale fundamental group of a scheme. Tau Ceti instantiates the same abstract theory for finite covering spaces of a topological space (`TauCeti.FiniteCoveringSpace.instGaloisCategory`, TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/Classification/GaloisCategory.lean:329), which is the topological analogue, not the arithmetic one.

targets.note: Absent, since neither fundamental group exists for a scheme.

targets.note: No arithmetic path torsor or Galois section exists in either library. The only base-point-change machinery is topological, for the fundamental group of a space.

targets.note: Absent; there is no tangential base point anywhere in the baseline.

IG.1 owns the geometric/arithmetic fundamental-group sequence, decomposition and inertia subgroups; NC.0's second target is its conclusion.
IG.6 says it will 'hand the profinite fundamental group and path torsors to the anabelian continuation', so path torsors are claimed on both sides of the boundary.

targets.note: Absent, and far out of reach at this baseline: neither library has an étale fundamental group, an outer Galois action, or hyperbolic curves. The words 'anabelian' and 'Mochizuki' do not occur in either library.

targets.note: Neither unipotent fundamental group exists. ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights.summary: The general height theory this roadmap needs as input is already in Mathlib, and more generally than the roadmap assumes: `Mathlib/NumberTheory/Height/` defines `AdmissibleAbsValues` — a family of absolute values satisfying the product formula with archimedean multiplicities — proves the product formula for every number field, builds multiplicative and logarithmic heights on tuples and on projectivizations, and proves the Northcott finiteness theorems `finite_setOf_mulHeight_nat_le` and `finite_setOf_logHeight₁_le` together with an abstract `Northcott` order class. Everything the roadmap actually owns is absent: `Arakelov`, `Faltings`, `Zarhin`, `arithmeticDegree`, `hermitianBundle` and `NeronModel` each have zero occurrences in the whole baseline, and the geometric inputs are missing too — there is no abelian scheme, no Néron or semistable model, no module of invariant differentials, no period lattice and no polarized moduli scheme. So no hermitian bundle, no arithmetic degree, no Hodge bundle with Faltings metric, no (stable) Faltings height, no isogeny formula and no theta-height comparison exists. The roadmap's own summary anticipates this correctly when it says general heights and Northcott 'are necessary but do not construct the stable Faltings height'; the audit's addition is that the necessary part is finished, in Mathlib, and that R35.1's product-formula target should simply be consumed rather than built.

targets.target: hermitian line and vector bundles over an arithmetic curve, with determinant, tensor and dual operations
targets.note: Absent from both libraries. `Arakelov`, `hermitianBundle` and any metrized-module carrier over `𝓞_K` have zero occurrences; the only invertible-sheaf theory in the baseline is Tau Ceti's `InvertibleSheaf`/`LineBundleClass` for schemes (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/LineBundle/), which carries no metric.

targets.target: arithmetic degree of a hermitian bundle, and comparison with the general height owner's normalization
targets.note: Absent; `arithmeticDegree` has zero occurrences.

targets.target: the product formula, with archimedean factors
targets.note: This target is fully in Mathlib and in more generality than asked: `AdmissibleAbsValues` axiomatizes a family of absolute values satisfying `∏_arch |x|_v · ∏_nonarch |x|_v = 1` with archimedean multiplicities, `Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/ProductFormula.lean` proves it for any number field, and `NumberField.instAdmissibleAbsValues` installs it. The archimedean weights are `totalWeight = [K:ℚ]`. The roadmap document treats the general-height layer as belonging to another owner (`ArithmeticHeights #287`) and does not claim it; the point of record is that it is already done in Mathlib.

targets.target: base-change and degree formulas for the height normalization under finite extension
targets.note: Mathlib has absolute multiplicative and logarithmic heights of tuples and of points of a projectivization, with invariance under scaling and coordinate permutation and explicit formulas over a number field and over `ℚ`. Invariance of the height under finite field extension is not stated as such, and there is no arithmetic-degree normalization to compare it with.

targets.target: the arithmetic intersection statements invoked by the moduli-height comparison
targets.note: Absent; there is no arithmetic intersection theory of any kind in either library.

duplicates.note: GZ.2 constructs the arithmetic intersection pairing on arithmetic surfaces from finite-place intersection lengths and archimedean Green functions — the same Arakelov machinery R35.1 needs, built for curves rather than for the moduli comparison.

RP.0 says it will 'Import normalized absolute heights, product formula and Northcott from the audited arithmetic-height supplier', so the product-formula and normalization targets appear in at least three roadmaps; Mathlib already supplies them.

targets.note: Absent. The nearest object is the invariant differential of a Weierstrass curve in Tau Ceti, a single differential on one affine model, not a determinant line bundle over a Dedekind base.

targets.target: the archimedean metric defined by integration at complex places, with positivity, basis-invariance and functoriality
targets.note: Absent. Nothing in the baseline integrates a differential form over the complex points of an abelian variety; there are no complex points of an abelian scheme to integrate over (see A5 of `AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli`).

targets.target: normalization under products and duals, and comparison with the elliptic period convention
targets.note: Absent; there is no period lattice of an elliptic curve in either library (the `period` declarations in the baseline are cusp widths and function periodicity in the modular-forms files).

R12.5 owns the Hodge bundle and Hecke normalization of differentials on modular curves, the relative-dimension-one case of this construction.

targets.note: Absent; `Faltings` has zero occurrences in either library, and neither input (the Hodge line of R35.2, the arithmetic degree of R35.1) exists.

What is missing is everything specific to this roadmap — the moduli points, and the constants relating their heights to the Faltings height.

ArithmeticDynamics.summary: The libraries supply this roadmap's two general inputs in full and almost nothing else. Mathlib's `Mathlib/Dynamics/PeriodicPts/` gives iteration, fixed and periodic points, minimal period and the divisibility calculus for an arbitrary self-map — more general than DY.0's morphisms of varieties, and at the level of maps rather than sampled points — and `Mathlib/NumberTheory/Height/` gives admissible absolute values with the product formula, logarithmic heights and Northcott finiteness over number fields. On top of those Tau Ceti has, for elliptic curves over any field with admissible absolute values, the complete Néron–Tate package DY.1 asks for in its abelian-variety acceptance example: the Tate limit with its convergence proved, the bounded difference from the naive height, the exact functional equation `ĥ(2P) = 4ĥ(P)`, quadraticity, and the theorem that canonical height zero is equivalent to torsion via Northcott. Everything else is missing, and mostly missing at the level of vocabulary: `Berkovich`, `dynatomic`, `equidistribution`, `arboreal`, `MordellLang` and `Lattès` each have zero occurrences in the whole baseline, and there is no self-map of `P¹` given by coprime forms, no dynamical degree or resultant of such a pair, no polarized morphism, no ample line bundle, no local height and no metrized line bundle. DY.1's general polarized construction, and DY.2–DY.6 entirely, are unbuilt; the sharpest overlap in the atlas is `GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.1`, which states DY.1's canonical-height targets for abelian varieties almost word for word.

targets.target: iteration of a self-map, orbit maps, periodic and preperiodic points
targets.note: Mathlib's `Mathlib/Dynamics/PeriodicPts/` develops iteration, `IsFixedPt`, `IsPeriodicPt`, `periodicPts`, minimal period and the whole divisibility calculus for an arbitrary self-map of a type, which covers the set-level content of this target in greater generality than a morphism of varieties. Because it is stated for `f : α → α` and `f^[n]`, an equality of iterates really is an equality of maps, satisfying the layer's acceptance criterion. What is not there is the scheme-theoretic layer: iteration of a morphism of varieties as a morphism, and orbit maps as morphisms.

targets.target: conjugacy of maps under automorphisms
targets.note: Mathlib has semiconjugacy of self-maps and transport of periodic points along it, which is the set-level statement; the dynamical notion of two rational maps being conjugate by an automorphism of `P¹`, and the invariants of that conjugacy class, are absent.

targets.target: rational functions on `P¹` given by coprime homogeneous forms, with degree, resultant and good reduction
targets.note: The resultant of two univariate polynomials exists in Mathlib with a Tau Ceti extension (Sylvester matrix, behaviour under `AdjoinRoot`, discriminant). There is no self-map of `P¹` presented by a pair of coprime homogeneous forms, no dynamical degree, no resultant of such a pair, and no dynamical good reduction; `HasGoodReduction` exists only for a Weierstrass curve at a prime. The required worked example — a map whose displayed resultant vanishes at a bad prime — has no carrier.

targets.target: for `f*L ≅ L^d` with `L` ample and `d > 1`, the canonical height as the limit `d^(-n) h_L(f^n P)`
targets.note: The Tate limiting construction is done in Tau Ceti for the doubling map on an elliptic curve over any field with `[Height.AdmissibleAbsValues F]` — so over any number field, not only ℚ. `canonicalHeight P = ½ lim h(2^n P)/4^n`, and the limit is proved to be attained, so the value is not `limUnder`'s junk value. The general polarized statement (arbitrary `f`, ample `L`, `f*L ≅ L^d`) is absent, because there is no ample line bundle, no `h_L`, and no polarized morphism in either library.

targets.target: the error bound `|ĥ - h| ≤ C`, the functional equation `ĥ(f P) = d · ĥ(P)`, and uniqueness
targets.note: The error bound and the functional equation are proved in the elliptic case: `canonicalHeight_two_nsmul` is `ĥ(2P) = 4 ĥ(P)`, the exact `d = 4` functional equation, and the parallelogram law upgrades it to full quadraticity with `ĥ(n • P) = n² ĥ(P)`. Uniqueness among bounded-error refinements is *not* stated as a named theorem in either library; it is used implicitly inside the limit argument (`tendsto_nhds_unique` at CanonicalHeight.lean:246) rather than exported.

targets.target: preperiodicity from zero canonical height, via Northcott
targets.note: This is fully proved in the case the layer's own acceptance criterion names — 'multiplication on an abelian variety' — for elliptic curves: a point has canonical height zero exactly when it is torsion, deduced from a `Northcott` instance for the canonical height that Tau Ceti derives from the naive height, which it in turn derives from Mathlib's field-height Northcott property. The other required example, the power map on `P¹`, has no carrier. The general polarized statement is absent.

targets.target: a separately stated theorem removing ampleness
targets.note: Absent, as is the ample case.

duplicates.note: GZ.1 states almost exactly DY.1's targets for abelian varieties: 'the canonical limit for symmetric bundles ... convergence, uniqueness among bounded-error quadratic refinements, addition and multiplication formulas, isogeny pullback ... positivity for ample symmetric bundles and characterize the zero locus as torsion over a number field using Northcott'. The duplication is essentially total on the abelian-variety side, which is one of DY.1's two acceptance examples.

RP.0 owns the height machine, canonical heights and the comparison of Néron–Tate with local heights; DY.1 declares it as a dependency, but the canonical-height limit and its error bound appear in both.

Layer 6 owns the naive height, the approximate parallelogram law and Northcott finiteness for elliptic curves — the layer whose targets Tau Ceti has actually built, and which supplies DY.1's elliptic instance.

targets.target: the Berkovich analytic carrier over a complete rank-one nonarchimedean field, with the dynamical maps constructed on it
targets.note: Absent: `Berkovich` has zero occurrences in either library. Tau Ceti has adic spaces (`TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/`, with `Spa` and continuous valuations), which is the Huber side of the comparison TB.0 owns, but no Berkovich spectrum of a Banach algebra.

targets.target: nonarchimedean local heights and escape rates
targets.note: Absent; there is no local height of any kind in either library.

targets.target: good reduction and reduction of cycles, with residue characteristic retained in multiplier and cycle formulas
targets.note: Absent for dynamical systems. Mathlib's reduction theory is only for Weierstrass curves (good/multiplicative/additive trichotomy); there is no multiplier of a periodic cycle and no reduction of a cycle.

duplicates.note: TB.0 owns the Berkovich spectrum and its comparison with the adic spectrum; DY.2 declares it consumes TB.0 and 'the dynamical maps are constructed on that carrier', so only the dynamics is owned here.

targets.target: dynatomic polynomials and schemes, with formal versus exact period, multiplier conditions and multiplicities
targets.note: Absent: `dynatomic` has zero occurrences. Mathlib's `Function.minimalPeriod` is the exact period of a point of a self-map, the set-level half of the formal/exact distinction, but there is no dynatomic polynomial whose roots would carry the formal period, and hence no multiplicity statement — so the layer's required worked example (a root with lower exact period but nontrivial dynatomic multiplicity) has no carrier.

targets.target: finiteness of the bounded-degree preperiodic set of a fixed polarized morphism
targets.note: Only the elliptic instance: torsion points are exactly the points of canonical height zero, and Northcott makes any bounded-height set finite over a number field. There is no finiteness statement for the preperiodic points of a general polarized morphism.

targets.target: certified enumeration of preperiodic points from effective height bounds
targets.note: Absent; there is no effective height bound or enumeration procedure in either library.

targets.target: an equidistribution theorem for semipositive adelic metrized line bundles
targets.note: Absent: `equidistribution` has zero occurrences in either library, and there is no adelic metrized line bundle.

targets.target: model metrics, semipositive approximation and local measures with total mass equal to the intersection degree
targets.note: Absent; these are the objects the layer declares it consumes from TB.6, and TB.6's targets are not in the libraries either — there is no formal model, no metric on a line bundle and no Chambert-Loir measure.

targets.target: dynamical energy, generic small-point hypotheses, and the application to a specified polarized system
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: TB.6 owns the model metrics, measures and local heights, and states explicitly that 'Equidistribution is a separate global theorem ... this stage provides its local analytic objects' — the boundary is drawn consistently from both sides.

targets.target: the rooted preimage tree of a point under iterated preimages, avoiding critical-orbit collisions
targets.note: Absent: `arboreal` has zero occurrences and there is no preimage tree of a dynamical system in either library. Mathlib has rooted trees and inverse limits as general structures, but nothing attaching one to a map.

targets.target: the continuous Galois action on the finite levels of the tree and on its inverse limit
targets.note: Only the abstract machinery: Mathlib's Galois-category API produces a profinite group acting continuously on finite sets, which is the shape of an arboreal representation, but there is no finite étale cover of a scheme to instantiate it with and no iterated-preimage tower.

targets.target: image and index statements from explicit ramification and irreducibility hypotheses, with a fully worked quadratic polynomial
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: IG.0 owns the profinite automorphism group of a fibre functor and its action on finite continuous sets, which DY.5 declares it imports for the Galois action on tree levels.

targets.target: family specialization maps and the comparison of canonical heights under the selected variation theorem
targets.note: Absent; there is no family of dynamical systems over a base and no specialization of canonical heights in either library.

targets.target: proved cases of dynamical Mordell–Lang and unlikely intersections, stated as separate source-bound endpoints
targets.note: Absent: `MordellLang` has zero occurrences in either library.

targets.target: complete power-map and elliptic/Lattès worked examples
targets.note: `Lattès` has zero occurrences. The elliptic side has real content — the canonical height of `n • P` is `n²` times that of `P`, and the Néron–Tate pairing is built from it as the polarization of a quadratic map — but it is stated for the group law, not for a Lattès map on `P¹`, and there is no power map on `P¹` at all.

targets.target: keeping dynamical Lehmer, uniform boundedness and unrestricted dynamical Mordell–Lang conjectural, with explicit conditional parameters
targets.note: A statement-hygiene requirement rather than a theorem; none of the three conjectures is stated in either library.
